parsed.title: Discussion on AI‑assisted job search, development tools, and code quality

topics.title: AI tools for job searching and résumé generation

claims.text: The user plans to set up OpenClaw to automate vacancy search, résumé generation and cover‑letter writing.
Automation that creates PDF résumés per vacancy is seen as useful because recruiters view the attached PDF during technical interviews.
Lack of AI‑related skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, embeddings, etc.) will cause recruiters to filter out candidates in 2026.
The market mainstream for AI tools started in 2025, with tools becoming good but very expensive.
The speaker expects the recruiter profession to disappear, preferring HR to handle personnel management.
Using GPT to generate SQL joins can produce large, inefficient queries (e.g., 450 lines of raw SQL pulling too much data, leading to 10‑20 min production queries).
Generated code may break projects; teams sometimes drop features entirely after review of AI‑generated code.
Some developers rely heavily on AI for routine tasks, claiming it dramatically speeds up development.
AI does not replace deep contextual knowledge held by an experienced developer.
Developers report that AI assistance lets them generate code (e.g., joins) quickly, reducing routine work and accelerating development.
The acceleration narrative originated around 2022 but became practical only after 2025.
